Stated Claim / Post Context:
Man critically injured in NYC beer bottle attack

A man was critically injured when he was hit in the head with a Dos Equis beer bottle in Washington Heights on Sunday morning, police said.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A man was critically injured when he was hit in the head with a Dos Equis beer bottle — possibly over a woman — in Washington Heights on Sunday morning, police said.

The Manhattan attack happened at West 190 Street and Saint Nicholas Avenue around 6:45 a.m. and left the victim unconscious, according to the NYPD.

A witness told The Post that he saw the victim, 43, and his assailant emerge from the nearby 24-hour fish market Calle 191 Pescaderia in fisticuffs before the bottle attack.

“There were guys fighting inside the fish market over a girl that works there,” said the witness, who declined to provide his name. “They came outside fighting,”

The wounded man was taken to Harlem Hospital. His unidentified attacker fled the scene and was still at large, officials said.

A street fruit vendor who works on the corner appeared unfazed by the assault.

“I was sleeping in my car. I heard the commotion. But that sort of stuff is normal here, so I just went back to sleep,” said the man, who also declined to give his name to The Post

The 12-ounce green bottle used to hit the victim was taken into evidence by officers on the scene, and a large pool of blood was visible on the sidewalk after the assault, photos showed.

More chaos then unfolded on the block while The Post was on the scene Sunday afternoon.

Shortly after 3 p.m., a gray Honda Accord was hit by a van while attempting to make an aburpt U-turn on Saint Nicholas Avenue between 189th and 190th streets.

There appeared to be no injuries, but the four occupants of the Honda fled the vehicle on foot immediately after the collision and were observed scattering in separate directions.

The Accord was apparently left in neutral when it was abandoned and then rolled backward before colliding with a third vehicle.
